title: Conjecture 1.2 (Coarse Menger conjecture for surfaces)
statement_text:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a fixed surface. For all integers $k,c\geq 0$ there exists $\ell>0$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a graph that embeds on $\mathcal{S}$ and let $S,T\subseteq V(G)$. Then either

$\bullet$ there are $k+1$ paths between $S,T$, pairwise $c$-distant; or

$\bullet$ there is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\leq k$ such that every path between $S,T$ contains a vertex with distance at most $\ell$ from some member of $X$.
context_text: Graphs are finite, without loops or parallel edges. The distance between two vertices, vertex sets or subgraphs is the number of edges of a shortest path with one end in each, and they are $c$-distant if their distance is at least $c$; a path between $S,T$ is a path with one end in $S$ and the other in $T$. Menger's theorem is the case $c=1$, $\ell=0$ (disjoint paths versus a separating set of $k$ vertices). The original coarse Menger conjecture, the same statement for all graphs, was proposed by Albrechtsen, Huynh, Jacobs, Knappe and Wollan, and independently by Georgakopoulos and Papasoglu; it holds for $k=1$, for $c=2$ in graphs of bounded degree, and for graphs of bounded path-width, but Nguyen, Scott and Seymour showed it false for all $k\ge2$, even with $c=3$ and maximum degree three (and even if $|X|$ may be an arbitrary function of $k$). Their counterexamples have unbounded genus, so the conjecture might hold for planar graphs or graphs on a fixed surface. As a first step, the authors prove it for planar $G$ drawn with all vertices of $S\cup T$ on the infinite region: then either there are $k+1$ paths between $S,T$ pairwise $(c+1)$-distant, or at most $k$ connected subgraphs, with diameters summing to at most $200k^3c$, meet every path between $S$ and $T$; in this case they also obtain a linear-time algorithm to test for $k+1$ pairwise far-apart paths.
notes: The paper proves a special case (Theorem 1.3): the conjecture holds when $G$ is planar and all vertices of $S\cup T$ lie on the infinite region, with the blocking structure being at most $k$ connected subgraphs whose diameters sum to at most $200k^3c$.
